phorbol ester activation of protein kinase (PK) C downregulates Na(+)/Ca(2+) exchanger (NCA) expression in renal epithelial LLC-MK(2) cells.
activation of protein kinase-C by phorbol ester downregulates expression of the sodium calcium exchanger in LLC-MK2 cells.
activation of PKCs with phorbol diesters downregulates NEX activity and transcript by 75 and 85%, respectively, in renal epithelial LLC-MK2 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein kinase C in the downregulation and the possible mechanism of downregulation of the Na+/Ca2+-exchanger (NCE).
the regulation of calcium reabsorption in renal epithelial LLC-MK2 cells.
the molecular mechanisms of Ca2+ reclamation by the nephron and the regulation of NCA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PKC activation by phorbol ester downregulates the NCE in LLC-MK2 cells by a process that involves a decrease in NCE mRNA and protein.
phorbol ester activation of protein kinase downregulates the sodium-calcium exchanger.
the activation of PKC by phorbol ester decreases expression of the NCE in renal epithelial cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phorbol ester activation of PKC decreases the expression of NCE mRNA and NCE protein, and decreases NCE activity in renal epithelia.

PKC is a key regulator of NCE.
